day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the direct train from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (€4.50, ~17 min), then make your way to Canal House Amsterdam to check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a self-guided walk along the Prinsengracht and Herengracht canals near your hotel. Explore the Jordaan neighborhood — one of Amsterdam's most charming and historic districts. Browse local boutiques, street art, and admire the iconic 17th-century canal houses for free.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to Leidseplein square to soak up the lively atmosphere. Explore the surrounding streets and get oriented with the city layout. End the evening with a relaxed walk back along the lit-up canals.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport or grab a quick snack on the train — skip formal breakfast this day.
meals.lunch: Grab a broodje (Dutch sandwich) from a local bakery or Albert Heijn supermarket near Centraal Station for €3–5.
meals.dinner: Eat at Dampkring Café area or try Foodhallen (a covered street food market) in the Jordaan for affordable local bites — budget €10–14.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light due to afternoon arrival. Use this time to rest, orient yourself, and pick up a GVB transit card or I Amsterdam City Card if planning heavy museum use. Supermarkets like Albert Heijn are great for cheap snacks and drinks throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Rijksmuseum when it opens at 9:00 AM to beat the crowds. Spend 2–3 hours exploring masterpieces by Rembrandt and Vermeer, plus Dutch Golden Age history. Book tickets online in advance to save time (€22.50 adult). The museum is a 15-min tram ride from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk next door to the Van Gogh Museum (€22 adult, book online). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring over 200 Van Gogh paintings and learning about his life and artistic journey. Afterward, relax in the adjacent Vondelpark — Amsterdam's beloved green space — completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Leidseplein area for dinner, then enjoy a budget-friendly evening exploring the vibrant Koningsplein and Spui squares. Browse the second-hand book market stalls if still open.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh stroopwafels and coffee from a street vendor or Albert Heijn near your hotel — €3–5.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the Museumplein area — try a herring sandwich (broodje haring) from a street cart for €4–6.
meals.dinner: Try Wok to Walk near Leidseplein for a filling Asian noodle box for €8–10, or visit Moeders restaurant for affordable Dutch classics around €12–15.

day_by_day.notes: Buy Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum tickets online at least a day in advance — they often sell out on weekends. Both museums are within walking distance of each other at Museumplein, making this a very efficient museum day.

day_by_day.morning: Book the Anne Frank House Tour (€16, must be booked online weeks in advance — check availability immediately!). The house is a short walk from Canal House Amsterdam. Arrive 10 minutes early. Allow 1.5 hours for this deeply moving and historically significant experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Anne Frank House, explore the surrounding Jordaan neighborhood on foot. Visit the Westerkerk church (free entry or small donation) — it has one of the best free views in Amsterdam from its tower (€9 for tower climb). Browse the Noordermarkt Sunday antiques and farmers market (free to browse).
day_by_day.evening: Take a budget Canal Boat Tour departing from near Centraal Station or the Jordaan area (€15–18 for a 1-hour guided tour). Cruising the UNESCO-listed canals at dusk is magical and very photogenic.

meals.breakfast: Visit Café Winkel 43 in the Jordaan for their famous Dutch apple pie and coffee — around €7–9.
meals.lunch: Pick up fresh produce and snacks from the Noordermarkt farmers market — budget €5–8 for a picnic-style lunch.
meals.dinner: Try De Vliegende Schotel, a well-known budget-friendly vegetarian restaurant in the Jordaan — mains around €12–15.

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House is the single most important booking of the trip — tickets sell out weeks in advance. If unavailable, the nearby Westerkerk and Jordaan walking tour still offer excellent historical context. Sunday markets in the Jordaan are a wonderful free cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Amsterdam Museum (now Amsterdam City Museum) or the free Stedelijk Museum garden area. Alternatively, explore the Dutch Resistance Museum (Verzetsmuseum, €16) — a powerful and underrated museum about WWII Dutch resistance, very relevant after visiting the Anne Frank House.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Plantage neighborhood and stroll through the Hortus Botanicus botanical garden (€11) — one of the oldest botanical gardens in the world, founded in 1638. Afterward, walk along the Amstel River and cross the iconic Magere Brug (Skinny Bridge) — free.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the lively De Pijp neighborhood to explore the Albert Cuyp Market (free, closes around 17:00 — arrive by 16:30). In the evening, enjoy the relaxed café culture of De Pijp, known as Amsterdam's 'Latin Quarter.'

meals.breakfast: Grab a simple breakfast at your hotel or pick up a croissant and coffee from a local bakery — €4–6.
meals.lunch: Eat at a De Pijp street food stall or grab a falafel wrap from one of the many affordable spots near Albert Cuypstraat — €5–8.
meals.dinner: Try Bazar Amsterdam in De Pijp — a colorful, affordable Middle Eastern restaurant with mains around €10–13. Very popular with locals.

day_by_day.notes: The Albert Cuyp Market is one of Europe's largest outdoor markets and completely free to browse — great for cheap Dutch snacks like stroopwafels, poffertjes, and fresh fruit. The Plantage area is easily walkable and less touristy than the city center, offering a more authentic Amsterdam experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the free Amsterdam Public Library (OBA) on Oosterdok for great city views from the rooftop terrace — completely free. Then explore the NEMO Science Museum exterior and the rooftop terrace (free access to the outdoor area with great harbor views). Walk along the Eastern Docklands waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to any favorite neighborhoods for last-minute exploration. Visit the Bloemenmarkt (floating flower market on the Singel canal) — free to browse, great for affordable souvenirs like tulip bulbs. Do any final souvenir shopping at budget-friendly spots around the Jordaan or Nine Streets (De 9 Straatjes).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell dinner in the city center. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Take a final evening canal walk to say goodbye to Amsterdam's beautiful waterways.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a proper Dutch breakfast at Café de Jaren overlooking the Amstel — €8–12.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap lunch from a FEBO automat (Dutch fast-food vending machine, a classic local experience) or a supermarket — €4–6.
meals.dinner: Visit Café 't Smalle in the Jordaan for a classic Dutch brown café experience — order bitterballen (fried snacks) and a local beer for around €12–15 total.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed (most hotels offer this for free). For the return journey, the train from Amsterdam Centraal to Schiphol runs every 10–15 minutes and takes about 17 minutes (€4.50). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security.

trip_options.title: Classic Amsterdam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Explore the Netherlands' premier art and history museum, home to masterpieces by Rembrandt, Vermeer, and other Dutch Golden Age painters. The collection spans 800 years of Dutch art and history across 80 galleries.

experiences.name: Jordaan Neighborhood Walking & Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through Amsterdam's most charming neighborhood, exploring its narrow streets, independent galleries, and boutique shops. Sample traditional Dutch street food including stroopwafels, raw herring, and Dutch cheese at local markets and hidden eateries.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight KL lands at 13:00, so no morning activity. Take the Amsterdam Airport Express (Sprinter) from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (~17 min, €5.40). Check in to Canal House Amsterdam, freshen up, and get oriented in your neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Canal Boat Tour — After settling in, join a 1-hour guided canal boat tour departing from near Centraal Station or the Jordaan area. Cruise the UNESCO-listed 17th-century canal ring, spot gabled merchant houses, and get a beautiful first impression of the city from the water. Tickets ~€15–18 pp.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the Jordaan neighborhood at golden hour — wander Prinsengracht and Brouwersgracht, browse boutique shop windows, and soak in the atmosphere. End the evening with dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and stroopwafel at Schiphol Airport before landing, or pick up a light snack at a bakery near the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Broodje Bert or a local café near Centraal Station — try a classic Dutch broodje (sandwich) with cheese or herring for ~€8–12.
meals.dinner: Café 't Smalle (Jordaan) — a cozy, historic brown café serving Dutch bites and hearty mains like stamppot or fish dishes. Budget ~€20–30 pp including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pre-book your Canal Boat Tour online to secure a late-afternoon slot. Validate your OV-chipkaart (public transit card) at the airport for easy travel all week. Canal House Amsterdam is ideally located in or near the Jordaan/canal belt, so most attractions are walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — Open at 9:00. Arrive early (9:00–9:30) to beat crowds. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring the Netherlands' premier art and history museum: Rembrandt's Night Watch, Vermeer's The Milkmaid, and the stunning Great Hall. Pre-book timed tickets online (~€22.50 pp). The museum is a 15-min walk or short tram ride from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum — Located directly next to the Rijksmuseum on Museumplein, this is the perfect afternoon follow-up. Explore the world's largest Van Gogh collection: over 200 paintings including The Bedroom and Almond Blossom. Allow 1.5–2 hours. Pre-book timed entry tickets (~€22 pp). Afterward, relax on Museumplein — bring a snack or grab a coffee at a nearby café.
day_by_day.evening: Leidseplein area for dinner and drinks — a lively square just a short walk from Museumplein with a great mix of restaurants and bars. Explore the vibrant nightlife or catch a live music performance at one of the venues.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Café Beurre (near Museumplein) — Dutch-style eggs, fresh bread, and coffee for ~€10–14.
meals.lunch: Grab lunch at the Rijksmuseum's café or from a food stall on Museumplein — sandwiches, salads, or Dutch pea soup (erwtensoep). Budget ~€12–16.
meals.dinner: Café Loetje (near Leidseplein) — famous for their perfectly cooked steaks and relaxed atmosphere. Mains ~€18–28 pp.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day at both museums — early arrival is essential. Book both museum tickets well in advance online. Consider the Museumkaart (€69.90) if you plan to visit 3+ museums during the trip — it pays for itself quickly and allows skip-the-line entry.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour — One of Amsterdam's most emotionally significant sites. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid from 1942–1944. Deeply moving and historically essential. Timed entry tickets must be booked months in advance (~€16 pp). Morning slots (9:00–10:30) are best for a quieter, more reflective experience. The house is a short walk from most canal-area hotels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Walking & Food Tour — After the solemnity of the Anne Frank House, transition into the charm of the Jordaan. Join a guided walking and food tour through Amsterdam's most picturesque neighborhood: narrow streets, independent galleries, antique shops, and local food tastings including Dutch cheese, herring, stroopwafels, and jenever (Dutch gin). Tours typically run 2.5–3 hours and cost ~€35–50 pp.
day_by_day.evening: Sunday markets wind down, so enjoy a quiet evening exploring the Nine Streets (De Negen Straatjes) — a grid of boutique-lined streets between the main canals. Browse unique shops before they close, then settle in for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Winkel 43 (Noordermarkt) — famous for their Dutch apple pie. On Sundays there's an organic farmers market at Noordermarkt nearby. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Food tastings on the Jordaan Food Tour count as lunch — you'll sample generous portions throughout. If still hungry, grab a kroket from a FEBO automat for a true Dutch street food experience (~€2–3).
meals.dinner: De Reiger (Jordaan) — a beloved local brown café with an excellent seasonal Dutch-French menu. Cozy, authentic, and mid-range. Mains ~€18–26 pp. Reserve ahead as it fills up.

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House tickets are notoriously difficult to get — book as early as possible (they release tickets 2 months in advance at 9:00 AM Amsterdam time). If tickets are unavailable, check for last-minute releases on the official website. The Jordaan Food Tour is best booked in advance through providers like Airbnb Experiences or GetYourGuide.

day_by_day.morning: Amsterdam Historical Museum / Amsterdam Museum — Dive deeper into the city's rich history, from its origins as a fishing village to its Golden Age as a global trading empire. The museum (Amsterdams Historisch Museum) offers fascinating exhibits on city life, trade, and culture. Entry ~€15 pp. Located in the city center, easily walkable. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Canal Belt on foot or by bike — Rent a bike (~€12–15/day from MacBike or Star Bikes) and cycle along the four main canals: Singel, Herengracht, Keizersgracht, and Prinsengracht. Stop at the Magere Brug (Skinny Bridge) over the Amstel River, explore the Jewish Quarter and the Portuguese Synagogue (~€17 pp), and visit Waterlooplein flea market for vintage finds and local character.
day_by_day.evening: Classical concert or cultural performance — Amsterdam has excellent affordable classical music. Check the Concertgebouw for free lunchtime concerts (though evening performances run ~€30–60 pp) or visit the Muziekgebouw for contemporary performances. Alternatively, enjoy a canal-side evening drink at a terrace bar.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at the hotel or at Scandinavian Embassy café — excellent specialty coffee and open-faced sandwiches. Budget ~€10–15.
meals.lunch: Grab lunch at Waterlooplein market area — falafel wraps, Dutch pancakes (poffertjes), or a sit-down lunch at a nearby café. Budget ~€10–15.
meals.dinner: Greetje (near Nieuwmarkt) — Amsterdam's best traditional Dutch restaurant with a modern twist. Try the Dutch beef stew or North Sea fish. Mains ~€22–32 pp. Reservations recommended.

day_by_day.notes: May in Amsterdam means long daylight hours (sunset ~21:15) — perfect for evening canal cycling or terrace sitting. If cycling feels daunting in city traffic, the canal belt is very walkable. The Portuguese Synagogue is a hidden gem and one of Europe's best-preserved 17th-century synagogues.

day_by_day.morning: Heineken Experience OR FOAM Photography Museum — Choose based on your mood. The Heineken Experience (~€23 pp, book online) is an interactive brewery tour inside the original 1867 Heineken building — fun, immersive, and includes tastings. FOAM Photography Museum (~€14 pp) is a world-class contemporary photography museum in a beautiful canal house — ideal for culture lovers wanting something quieter. Both are centrally located.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final canal stroll and souvenir shopping — Spend your last afternoon revisiting favorite spots. Browse the Bloemenmarkt (floating flower market on the Singel) for Dutch tulip bulbs and souvenirs. Walk along Herengracht (the 'Golden Bend') to admire the grandest 17th-century merchant mansions. Stop at a local cheese shop (like Abraham Kef in the Jordaan) to pick up aged Gouda or Edam to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special restaurant — treat yourself to a memorable last meal before departure.

meals.breakfast: Full Dutch breakfast at the hotel — take your time on the last morning. Or visit Bakers & Roasters for a hearty brunch (eggs, avocado toast, fresh juices). Budget ~€12–18.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a canal-side café — try Dutch pancakes (pannenkoeken) at Pancakes Amsterdam near the Jordaan. Budget ~€12–16.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Vinkeles or Rijsel — Vinkeles is a refined Dutch-French tasting menu in a historic bakery (splurge option, ~€65–90 pp). Rijsel is a more relaxed but equally acclaimed Flemish-French bistro (~€25–35 pp). Both are excellent farewell dinner choices. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Check your departure details for Day 6 — if flying early, pack the night before and confirm the Sprinter train schedule to Schiphol (runs every 15 min, ~17 min journey). Keep your OV-chipkaart loaded. Store luggage at the hotel until checkout if needed. Amsterdam Airport is efficient — arrive 2 hours before departure for European flights, 3 hours for intercontinental.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Schiphol to Canal House Amsterdam via a chauffeured Mercedes-Benz or similar premium vehicle (~30 minutes). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your elegantly appointed canal-view suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Canal Boat Tour (14:30–16:30): Begin your Amsterdam experience with a private guided canal boat tour along the UNESCO-listed canal ring. Departing near the hotel, glide past the iconic 17th-century merchant houses, drawbridges, and hidden courtyards of the Golden Age. A knowledgeable private guide provides historical and architectural commentary throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Herengracht and Keizersgracht canals at golden hour, taking in the illuminated bridges and reflections on the water. Afterward, enjoy a relaxed first dinner at a top-tier Amsterdam restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or at airport upon arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments and afternoon tea arranged at Canal House Amsterdam upon check-in, or a quick artisan bite at Lot Sixty One Coffee Roasters nearby
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ciel Bleu (Hotel Okura, 2 Michelin stars) — contemporary French-Dutch haute cuisine with panoramic city views; reserve the tasting menu with wine pairing for a truly luxurious first evening

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer before arrival. Confirm Canal Boat Tour booking in advance, requesting a private vessel for an exclusive experience. Ciel Bleu reservation should be made weeks ahead given high demand.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit (09:00–12:00): Beat the crowds with an early-access private guided tour of the Netherlands' premier art and history museum. Marvel at Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and Delftware collections. Your expert art historian guide provides in-depth context on the Dutch Golden Age. Stroll through the museum's stunning garden afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum (13:30–16:00): A short walk from the Rijksmuseum, immerse yourself in the world's largest Van Gogh collection — over 200 paintings and 500 drawings. Opt for a private guided experience to explore the emotional depth of works like 'The Bedroom' and 'Almond Blossom.' Afterward, explore the chic boutiques and galleries around the Museumplein and PC Hooftstraat, Amsterdam's luxury shopping street.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to refresh before an elegant evening out. Take a leisurely walk along the Prinsengracht canal as the city lights come on.

meals.breakfast: Sumptuous breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam's dining room, featuring fresh Dutch cheeses, smoked salmon, artisan breads, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Loetje (Museum Quarter) — renowned for its premium Dutch steak sandwiches and terrace dining, beloved by Amsterdam's discerning locals
meals.dinner: Dinner at De Librije's Zusje Amsterdam (Waldorf Astoria, 2 Michelin stars) — inventive Dutch-Nordic cuisine in a stunning canal-side setting; opt for the chef's tasting menu with natural wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum skip-the-line private tours in advance — Saturday crowds can be significant. PC Hooftstraat hosts flagship stores of Hermès, Chanel, and Rolex if luxury retail is of interest.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour (09:00–11:00): A profoundly moving and essential Amsterdam experience. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during World War II. A private or small-group guided tour provides historical depth and emotional context. Timed entry tickets must be secured well in advance. Located in the Jordaan district, just a short walk from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Walking & Food Tour (12:30–15:30): Transition seamlessly from reflection to celebration of Amsterdam's most charming neighborhood. Wander narrow cobblestone streets, browse independent galleries and antique shops, and sample local delicacies — Dutch stroopwafels, artisan cheeses, raw herring, and craft jenever (Dutch gin) — guided by a local food and culture expert. Visit the picturesque Bloemgracht and Egelantiersgracht canals.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Nine Streets (De Negen Straatjes) — a boutique-lined area connecting the main canals — for curated shopping or gallery browsing. Enjoy a pre-dinner cocktail at a classic Amsterdam brown café (bruine kroeg) such as Café 't Smalle, one of the city's oldest.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam, followed by a specialty flat white at Scandinavian Embassy café en route to the Anne Frank House
meals.lunch: Premium bites included in the Jordaan Food Tour (artisan cheese, charcuterie, local specialties). Supplement with a stop at Buffet van Odette for homemade Dutch quiches and soups
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Breda — sophisticated modern European cuisine in a beautifully restored Jordaan townhouse; seasonal tasting menu with sommelier-curated wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House tickets must be booked online months in advance — Sunday slots fill extremely quickly. The Jordaan Food Tour is best experienced on Sunday when the Noordermarkt organic farmers' market is also active (morning hours).

day_by_day.morning: Private Cultural Immersion — Amsterdam's Historic Center & Golden Age Architecture (09:30–12:00): Embark on a private walking tour of Amsterdam's historic center with a specialist guide. Explore the Royal Palace on Dam Square, the Nieuwe Kerk, and the intricate step-gabled facades of the Herengracht's 'Golden Bend' — the most prestigious address in 17th-century Amsterdam. Visit the Amsterdam Museum or the Allard Pierson Museum for deeper historical context on the city's origins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Rijksmuseum Art Atelier Experience or Delft Blue Workshop (13:30–16:00): Participate in an exclusive hands-on Dutch cultural experience — either a private art workshop inspired by Dutch Masters at a studio near the Rijksmuseum, or a premium Delftware painting session with a master craftsman. Alternatively, visit the Foam Photography Museum or the Stedelijk Museum for world-class contemporary art. End the afternoon with a private canal kayak or stand-up paddleboard experience along the quieter eastern canals.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks aboard a private canal boat hired for a twilight cruise with champagne and Dutch bitterballen, floating past the illuminated Magere Brug (Skinny Bridge) and Amstel River.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Canvas (Volkshotel rooftop) for panoramic city views, or continue with the hotel's curated breakfast service
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Greetje — the finest traditional Dutch cuisine in Amsterdam, using seasonal local ingredients; try the pea soup, North Sea sole, and Dutch apple cake
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rijsel — a beloved Amsterdam institution in a converted school gymnasium, serving exceptional Flemish rotisserie chicken and refined Belgian-Dutch bistro fare; relaxed yet premium atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The private twilight canal cruise should be pre-booked through a luxury charter company such as Those Dam Boat Guys or a hotel concierge-arranged private vessel. Ensure champagne and canapés are pre-ordered for the cruise.

day_by_day.morning: Hermitage Amsterdam Area & Eastern Docklands Exploration (09:30–11:30): Discover Amsterdam's lesser-known architectural gem — the Eastern Docklands (Oostelijk Havengebied), featuring avant-garde residential architecture on Java Island and KNSM Island. Walk across the iconic Python Bridge and explore the NEMO Science Museum's rooftop terrace for sweeping views over the harbor and city skyline. A peaceful, crowd-free contrast to the historic center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Leisure & Luxury Shopping (12:00–15:00): Return to the city center for last-minute exploration. Browse the elegant antique dealers along Nieuwe Spiegelstraat, visit a premium Dutch diamond house (Gassan Diamonds offers private tours), or revisit a favorite canal-side spot for quiet reflection. Pack, check out, and arrange a private transfer to Schiphol Airport or onward destination.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner before departure, or airport lounge experience at Schiphol's exclusive Aspire Lounge / KLM Crown Lounge if departing this evening.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — request a special farewell spread with Dutch cheeses, smoked eel, fresh stroopwafels, and champagne if celebrating
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Rijksmuseum's Grand Café Cobra or a final terrace lunch at Restaurant Momo (Asian-European fusion) on the Hobbemastraat — sophisticated, relaxed, and perfect for a last Amsterdam afternoon
meals.dinner: If departing late: dinner at Bord'Eau (Hotel de l'Europe, 1 Michelin star) — French-Dutch fine dining on the Amstel River with impeccable service and a legendary wine cellar; a perfect farewell to Amsterdam

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with Canal House Amsterdam and arrange luggage storage if needed for afternoon activities. Private transfer to Schiphol should be booked 24 hours in advance. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure given Schiphol's premium security and check-in procedures.
